title: RIOJA. Complex Dusty Starbursts in a Major Merger B14-65666 at z = 7.15
question: Investigate the spatially resolved stellar, gaseous, and dusty properties in morphology and star formation of the bright major-merger galaxy system B14-65666 at z = 7.15 during the epoch of reionization by combining JWST NIRCam and ALMA observations.

data.bands: Band 6 (rest-frame 158.7 um), Band 7 (rest-frame 122.6 um), Band 8 (rest-frame 88.84 um)
data.angular_resolution: Band 6: 0.28x0.20 arcsec (or 0.29x0.23 arcsec); Band 7: 1.17x0.98 arcsec (or 1.15x0.97 arcsec); Band 8: 0.39x0.36 arcsec (or 0.39x0.37 arcsec)
data.sensitivity: 5-sigma depth: Band 8 = 141 uJy/beam, Band 7 = 45.5 uJy/beam, Band 6 = 42.3 uJy/beam

what.value: ALMA Band 6 and Band 8 continuum flux densities, [O III] 88 um line fluxes, and IR luminosities L_IR

evidence.loc: Summary of Previous Observations of B14-65666

recipe.goal: Reduce JWST NIRCam images and align astrometry
recipe.method: Reduce NIRCam data using custom pipeline based on JWST pipeline v1.9.4 with snowball/wisp removal and 1/f background homogenization, then align astrometry to three Gaia DR3 stars.

recipe.goal: Homogenize PSFs, resample images, and measure aperture photometry and optical [O III] line map
recipe.method: Construct effective PSFs using photutils, create convolution kernels with PyPHER to match F444W (or ALMA clean beam), resample with reproject, perform fixed-aperture photometry with local sky annulus subtraction, and derive optical [O III] flux map from F356W-F444W excess.
key_parameters: Component apertures: E = 1.4x0.80, W = 1.1x0.66, E-core = 0.44x0.44, W-core = 0.44x0.44, N-tail = 0.70x0.40, S-tail = 1.0x0.50 arcsec^2
assumptions: 5% absolute flux uncertainty included in photometric uncertainties

recipe.goal: Perform UV-to-FIR SED fitting for total system and resolved components
recipe.method: Fit NIRCam photometry with and without ALMA Band 6, 7, 8 dust continuum and [O III] 88 um line fluxes using Bagpipes with BPASS v2.3 stellar models, CLOUDY nebular emission, and CIGALE Draine et al. (2014) dust emission models.
key_parameters: n_H = 100 cm^-3 (fixed in Bagpipes CLOUDY models)
Old stellar component: constant SF from 600 to 100 Myr ago with Z_star = 0.5 Z_sun
Dust parameters fixed: alpha_U = 2, U_max = 10^7, q_PAH = 2.5%
assumptions: Kroupa (2001) IMF from 0.1 to 300 M_sun and BPASS Delta log(alpha/Fe) = +0.6
Gas-phase metallicity identical to stellar metallicity

recipe.method: Compute monochromatic UV luminosity L_UV at 1600 A and UV spectral slope beta_UV via linear fitting to 500 posterior SED models (from NIRCam-only fits) in Calzetti et al. (1994) windows, combine with ALMA L_IR from Hashimoto et al. (2019), and compare against canonical Meurer and SMC relations.
assumptions: Modified blackbody T_d = 48 K and beta_d = 2.0 for L_IR

recipe.goal: Construct optical-to-FIR [O III] line ratio map and model gas-phase metallicity
recipe.method: Correct F356W and F444W images for dust attenuation using best-fit A_V, convolve optical [O III] map to ALMA 0.38'' beam, divide by ALMA [O III] 88 um moment-0 map, and compare ratios with CLOUDY v17.02 photoionization models as a function of Z_gas, U, and n_e (computed with PyNeb).
key_parameters: Aperture dust attenuation corrections: E (A_V = 1.2 mag), W (0.34 mag), E-core (0.72 mag)
CLOUDY stopping criterion: electron fraction = 10^-2; SFH = 10-Myr constant star formation
assumptions: Plane-parallel geometry under constant pressure; electron density n_e ~ 200-400 cm^-3; T_e = 1.2x10^4 K for PyNeb n_e calculation

score_reason: All ALMA and JWST datasets are public, full photometry tables (Table 2) and SED prior ranges (Table 5) are explicitly provided, and standard open-source tools (Bagpipes, CLOUDY, photutils, PyPHER) are used; however, exact aperture coordinates/orientations and the custom Bagpipes+CIGALE+BPASS integration scripts are not released.
rediscovery_reason: Public JWST and ALMA archival data, complete photometric tables, and clearly specified SED fitting and CLOUDY modeling parameters make the main numeric results (stellar masses, SFRs, beta_UV, and [O III] line ratios/metallicities) well-suited for reproduction.
